payload.title: CI auth: GitHub OIDC provider and per-site CI roles; GitHub App connection runbook
payload.description:
## Goal
GitHub Actions in a publication repo can call AWS (deploy `infra/`, `aws amplify start-job`, content CLI jobs) with GitHub OIDC and least privilege, with no stored AWS keys; and the per-site runbook records the Amplify GitHub App connection. Implements the "No long-lived tokens" table of docs/standard-site.md 1.6 for CI.

## Context (verified)
- Nothing OIDC exists in the repo today (`rg -n "OpenIdConnect|oidc" infra amplify .github` is empty; the only workflow is `inbound-email-tests.yml`). Account `335163751677`, `us-east-1`. The app-shell stack (`infra/amplify-app-shell/lib/amplify-app-shell.ts`, `PPY-39f928` reshapes it) creates the service and compute roles.
- Account-global singleton: `AWS::IAM::OidcProvider` for `token.actions.githubusercontent.com` can exist only once per account, so it must not live in a per-site stack.
- Trust format (docs/standard-site.md 1.6): `repo:AnthusAI/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/<branch>`.
- Decision (YAGNI): one CI role per site with an `infra` permission set limited to: `amplify:StartJob/ListJobs/GetJob/ListBranches` on the site's apps, `ssm:GetParameter(s)` on the site's secret paths (for `papyrus auth refresh-jwt`), `cloudformation:*` on `amplify-app-shell-<siteId>` only if the site deploys infra from CI (flag `ciCanDeployInfra`, default false), plus read-only `sts:GetCallerIdentity`. No `AdministratorAccess`. Package publishing uses npm/PyPI trusted publishing (`PPY-78e818`), not AWS.

## Exact changes
1. `infra/amplify-app-shell/lib/github-oidc-provider.ts` (new construct `GithubOidcProviderStack`, exported from `@anthusai/papyrus/infra`, with a CLI `papyrus-infra synth --account-stack github-oidc`): creates `iam.OpenIdConnectProvider("GithubOidc", { url: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com", clientIds: ["sts.amazonaws.com"] })`. Deployed ONCE per account by a human; before creating, the doc tells to check `aws iam list-open-id-connect-providers` and import instead if it exists.
2. In `AmplifyAppShellStack` (`PPY-39f928` config adds `github: { owner: "AnthusAI", repo: "<repo>", branches?: string[] (default ["main","staging"]), ciCanDeployInfra?: boolean }`): create `ciRole` (`RoleName: "<siteId>-github-ci"`) assumed by the account's existing OIDC provider (looked up with `iam.OpenIdConnectProvider.fromOpenIdConnectProviderArn(arn:aws:iam::<account>:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com)`) with conditions `StringEquals token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud = sts.amazonaws.com` and `StringLike token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub in [repo:AnthusAI/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/<branch>...]`; `maxSessionDuration` 1 h; inline policy per the decision above. Output the role ARN.
3. `docs/site-hosting.md` section "CI access without keys": workflow snippet
   ```yaml
   permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
   steps:
     - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
       with: { role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::335163751677:role/<siteId>-github-ci, aws-region: us-east-1 }
     - run: aws amplify start-job --app-id <id> --branch-name main --job-type RELEASE
   ```
   and the runbook checklist per site: GitHub App connected for each app (date), OIDC role ARN, secrets live in SSM only, PAT secret deleted.
4. `scripts/verify-oidc-role.sh <role-arn>` (human-run proof, not CI): documents how to prove allowed/denied actions (below).

## Data shapes
Trust policy statement (synth output):
```json
{ "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::335163751677:oidc-provider/token.actions.githubusercontent.com" },
  "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
  "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com" },
                 "StringLike": { "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub": ["repo:AnthusAI/Pilobol.us:ref:refs/heads/main", "repo:AnthusAI/Pilobol.us:ref:refs/heads/staging"] } } }
```

## Tests
- Synth assertions added to `scripts/test-infra-synth.mjs` (from `PPY-39f928`): the CI role's trust policy has exactly the `sub` list built from `github.branches`, `aud` is `sts.amazonaws.com`, no `Resource: "*"` with `Action: "*"`, no wildcard `sub` (`repo:AnthusAI/*` is rejected by `parseSiteConfig`).
- Unit: `parseSiteConfig` rejects `github.branches` containing `*` and an owner other than a plain GitHub login.
- No Gherkin.
- Human proof (needs a real repo and AWS): a throwaway workflow in a scratch repo assumes the role and runs `aws amplify list-jobs --app-id <id> --branch-name main` (allowed) and `aws iam list-users` (must fail `AccessDenied`); a run from a non-listed branch fails to assume the role. Paste the run URLs in the ticket.

## Acceptance checks
- `node scripts/test-infra-synth.mjs` passes with the new assertions.
- `papyrus-infra synth --account-stack github-oidc` produces a template with one `Custom::AWSCDKOpenIdConnectProvider` (or `AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider`).
- After Ryan deploys the provider (below) and the site stack: the scratch workflow proves allowed and denied actions.

## Dependencies
Blocked by `PPY-39f928` (shared construct file `lib/amplify-app-shell.ts`, config schema) and `PPY-78e818` (package exports). Blocks Phase 3 CI setup per site. Not blocking the other Phase 2 tickets.

## Risks
- A second `OpenIdConnectProvider` for the same URL fails; check for an existing one first (the account may already have one from other projects).
- Condition keys must match the actual `sub` GitHub emits (environment-scoped jobs emit `repo:<o>/<r>:environment:<name>`; do not use GitHub environments in these workflows, or add that form deliberately).
- `ciCanDeployInfra` gives CloudFormation power on one stack: keep it false until a site needs it.

## Needs Ryan
1. Deploy the account-level provider once: `AWS_PROFILE=legacy` (see the memory/AGENTS.local.md profile guidance) `cdk deploy GithubOidcProviderStack` from the scratch infra app after `aws iam list-open-id-connect-providers` shows none for `token.actions.githubusercontent.com`.
2. The Amplify GitHub App connection per app (click path in `PPY-39f928`'s ticket) and recording it in each site's runbook.

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-e7f81e-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).
